newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Randstad sees 1996 net profit up 25 pct. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Randstad sees 1996 net profit up 25 pct. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]

text.p: Temporary employment agency Randstad NV said on Monday it expected 1996 net profit to have risen by some 25 percent compared with 1995.
In 1995, the company posted a net of 163.3 (corrects figure from 112.4) million guilders and in August it had said it expected full-year 1996 earnings to rise some 20 percent.
Analysts expected the company to report a rise of the preliminary 1996 net profit of 24 percent to about 203 million guilders.
Randstad said 1996 turnover had risen by 25 percent to six billion guilders from 4.7 billion while net profit had risen at a "comparable" rate and had thus exceeded its expectations.
The company said the temporary employment market had grown in all of the countries where it operates in 1996, except for France, and that its market share had risen everywhere.
Randstad said its security, information technology and transport operations had also achieved considerably better results in 1996.
The number of Randstad offices rose to 965 at the end of 1996 from 895 at the end of 1995, with most new offices added in the Netherlands and Germany. Average turnover per office rose.
Randstad said it would publish full 1996 results and its dividend proposal on February 28.
